'''Volkmar Braun''' (born 18 July 1938) is a German biochemist and microbiologist. He held a chair of microbiology at the [[University of Tübingen]] from 1974 to 2007, and was afterwards a Max Planck Fellow at the Max Planck Institute for Developmental Biology in Tübingen.

Braun's research mainly concerned the outer membrane of ''[[Escherichia coli]]''. In 1969 he discovered a lipoprotein covalently bound to the peptidoglycan layer of the cell envelope, now known as [[Braun's lipoprotein]]. He later studied how iron compounds and protein toxins are carried across the outer membrane, which has no energy source of its own. With Robert E. W. Hancock he showed that the proton motive force of the inner membrane provides the energy for transport across the outer membrane. He described surface signaling, a form of gene regulation in which a signal received at the cell surface is transmitted to the cytoplasm, where a sigma factor is activated. He also studied the structure, mode of action and uptake of bacterial protein toxins: colicins, pesticin, and the hemolysin of ''[[Serratia marcescens]]''.

== Early life and education ==
Braun was born on 18 July 1938 in [[Ravensburg]], Germany.<ref name="HAdW">{{cite web |title=Volkmar Braun |url=https://en.hadw-bw.de/akademie/mitglieder/volkmar-braun |publisher=Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities |access-date=11 September 2026}}</ref> He studied chemistry at the [[University of Freiburg]] and [[LMU Munich]]<ref name="Leo2008">{{cite web |title=Volkmar Braun |url=https://www.leopoldina.org/fileadmin/Migrierte_Daten/Publikationen/Dokumente/mitg2008.pdf |work=Neugewählte Mitglieder 2008 |publisher=Deutsche Akademie der Naturforscher Leopoldina |language=de |access-date=11 September 2026}}</ref> and carried out his diploma and doctoral research at the [[Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry]] in Munich under Gerhard Braunitzer and [[Adolf Butenandt]]. He received his doctorate from LMU Munich in 1965.<ref name="Leo2008" />

== Career ==
By January 1966 Braun was a research fellow in the biochemistry department of the [[California Institute of Technology]] in Pasadena.<ref name="VanNuys1966">{{cite news |title=German Scientist to Address Group at City College |newspaper=The Van Nuys News and Valley Green Sheet |location=Van Nuys, California |date=11 January 1966 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-van-nuys-news-and-valley-green-sheet/205738664/}}</ref> From 1966 to 1971 he was a scientific assistant at the Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry in Munich and at the Max Planck Institute of Biology in Tübingen,<ref name="Braun2022">{{cite journal |last1=Braun |first1=Volkmar |title=Transkriptionskontrolle über bakterielle Membranen |journal=BIOspektrum |date=2022 |volume=28 |issue=4 |pages=374–376 |language=de |doi=10.1007/s12268-022-1778-6|doi-access=free }}</ref> before moving to the [[Max Planck Institute of Molecular Genetics]] in Berlin.<ref name="Leo2008" /> He was at the Berlin institute from 1971 to 1974.<ref name="MPIMG2014">{{cite book |editor-last=Vingron |editor-first=Martin |title=Gene und Menschen: 50 Jahre Forschung am Max-Planck-Institut für molekulare Genetik |date=2014 |publisher=Max-Planck-Institut für molekulare Genetik |location=Berlin |language=de |pages=17, 40 |url=https://www.molgen.mpg.de/3507652/50_Jahre_MPIMG_screen_komplett_deN.pdf}}</ref> In 1974 he was appointed to a chair of microbiology at the University of Tübingen, named Microbiology/Membrane Physiology, which he held until his retirement in 2007.<ref name="Wohlleben2012">{{cite journal |last1=Wohlleben |first1=Wolfgang |title=Microbiology at the University of Tübingen |journal=BIOspektrum |date=2012 |issue=Tagungsband zur VAAM-Jahrestagung 2012 |pages=23–27 |issn=0947-0867 |url=https://vaam.de/media/tagungsband_2012.pdf}}</ref> He then held a six-year appointment as a Max Planck Fellow at the Max Planck Institute for Developmental Biology in Tübingen,<ref name="Wohlleben2012" /><ref name="MPIMG2014" /> where he worked in the protein department headed by [[Andrei Lupas]].<ref name="HAdW" />

== Research ==
Braun discovered a lipoprotein covalently bound to the murein (peptidoglycan) layer of the ''E. coli'' cell envelope. He reported it in 1969.<ref name="Asmar2018">{{cite journal |last1=Asmar |first1=Abir T |last2=Collet |first2=Jean-François |title=Lpp, the Braun lipoprotein, turns 50—major achievements and remaining issues |journal=FEMS Microbiology Letters |date=1 September 2018 |volume=365 |issue=18 |article-number=fny199 |doi=10.1093/femsle/fny199 |quote=We dedicate this...discoverer of Lpp; In 1969, V. Braun...every 10 repeating units.|hdl=2078.1/209405 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> The protein is attached to the peptidoglycan by a lysine residue and can be released by trypsin, which hydrolyses that bond.<ref name="Salton1971">{{cite journal |last1=Salton |first1=MRJ |title=Bacterial membranes |journal=CRC Critical Reviews in Microbiology |date=1971 |volume=1 |issue=1 |pages=161–197 |doi=10.3109/10408417109104480|quote=The lipoprotein which Braun...bond with trypsin.}}</ref><ref name="Asmar2018" /> It was sequenced by him and Valerie Bosch in 1972 and they found it very repetitive. Shortly afterwards Klaus Hantke determined the lipid structure, an S-glyceryl-cysteine residue carrying three fatty acids attached to the N-terminal cysteine.<ref name="Asmar2018" /><ref name="Nakayama2012">{{cite journal |last1=Nakayama |first1=H |last2=Kurokawa |first2=K |last3=Lee |first3=BL |title=Lipoproteins in bacteria: structures and biosynthetic pathways |journal=The FEBS Journal |date=2012 |volume=279 |issue=23 |pages=4247–4268 |doi=10.1111/febs.12041|quote=In 1973, Hantke...at its N-terminus.}}</ref> It became known as [[Braun's lipoprotein]].<ref name="Nakayama2012" /> The repetitive sequence he reported in 1972 was later shown to form an α-helical coiled coil, which was not recognised at the time.<ref name="Lupas2017">{{cite book |last1=Lupas |first1=AN |last2=Bassler |first2=J |last3=Dunin-Horkawicz |first3=S |chapter=The structure and topology of α-helical coiled coils |editor1-last=Parry |editor1-first=DAD |editor2-last=Squire |editor2-first=JM |title=Fibrous Proteins: Structures and Mechanisms |series=Subcellular Biochemistry |volume=82 |date=2017 |pages=95–129 |publisher=Springer |doi=10.1007/978-3-319-49674-0_4|quote=As an intriguing aside...only recognized years later}}</ref>

Braun and colleagues isolated the outer membrane protein then known as TonA, now FhuA, which is involved in ferrichrome-dependent iron uptake and also serves as the receptor for phages T1, T5 and φ80 and for colicin M.<ref name="Ghuysen1977">{{cite book |last=Ghuysen |first=Jean-Marie |chapter=Biosynthesis and assembly of bacterial cell walls |editor1-last=Poste |editor1-first=George |editor2-last=Nicolson |editor2-first=Garth L |title=The Synthesis, Assembly and Turnover of Cell Surface Components |series=Cell Surface Reviews |volume=4 |date=1977 |pages=463–595 |publisher=North-Holland |location=Amsterdam|quote=This protein has been...and for colicin M.}}</ref> They showed that FhuA functions as a gated channel requiring energy for phage entry.<ref name="Marantos2026">{{cite journal |last1=Marantos |first1=A |last2=Sneppen |first2=K |last3=Brown |first3=S |last4=Mitarai |first4=N |title=Viral commitment to infection depends on host metabolism |journal=eLife |date=2026 |volume=14 |page=RP107825 |doi=10.7554/eLife.107825 |doi-access=free|quote=Braun's research established...phage entry.}}</ref> Although the outer membrane contains no energy source of its own,<ref name="Llamas2014">{{cite journal |last1=Llamas |first1=MA |last2=Imperi |first2=F |last3=Visca |first3=P |last4=Lamont |first4=IL |title=Cell-surface signaling in ''Pseudomonas'': stress responses, iron transport, and pathogenicity |journal=FEMS Microbiology Reviews |date=2014 |volume=38 |issue=4 |pages=569–597 |doi=10.1111/1574-6976.12078|quote=The iron–siderophore complexes...energy available}}</ref> the irreversible adsorption of phages T1 and φ80 to ''E. coli'' requires energy, and in 1976 Braun and Robert E. W. Hancock showed that it comes from the proton motive force of the cytoplasmic membrane.<ref name="Silale2023">{{cite journal |last1=Silale |first1=A |last2=van den Berg |first2=B |title=TonB-dependent transport across the bacterial outer membrane |journal=Annual Review of Microbiology |date=2023 |volume=77 |pages=67–88 |doi=10.1146/annurev-micro-032421-111116|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="Swayne2011">{{cite journal |last1=Swayne |first1=C |last2=Postle |first2=K |title=Taking the ''Escherichia coli'' TonB transmembrane domain "offline"? Nonprotonatable Asn substitutes fully for TonB His20 |journal=Journal of Bacteriology |date=2011 |volume=193 |issue=15 |pages=3693–3701 |doi=10.1128/JB.05219-11|quote=This unusual arrangement...Escherichia coli bacteriophages.|pmc=3147502 }}</ref> He proposed that the ''tonB'' product couples metabolic energy to the outer membrane receptor proteins,<ref name="Gudmundsdottir1989">{{cite journal |last1=Gudmundsdottir |first1=A |last2=Bell |first2=PE |last3=Lundrigan |first3=MD |last4=Bradbeer |first4=C |last5=Kadner |first5=RJ |title=Point mutations in a conserved region (TonB box) of ''Escherichia coli'' outer membrane protein BtuB affect vitamin B12 transport |journal=Journal of Bacteriology |date=1989 |volume=171 |issue=12 |pages=6526–6533 |doi=10.1128/jb.171.12.6526-6533.1989|quote=Braun and colleagues...membrane receptor proteins|pmc=210543 }}</ref> and he and his colleagues named the "TonB box", the conserved pentapeptide at the N terminus of TonB-dependent transporters, which is also present in the TonB-dependent colicins.<ref name="Silale2023" /><ref name="Cascales2007" /> They further showed that the TolR and TolQ proteins can substitute in vivo, to some extent, for ExbD and ExbB.<ref name="GarciaHerrero2007">{{cite journal |last1=Garcia-Herrero |first1=A |last2=Peacock |first2=RS |last3=Howard |first3=SP |last4=Vogel |first4=HJ |title=The solution structure of the periplasmic domain of the TonB system ExbD protein reveals an unexpected structural homology with siderophore-binding proteins |journal=Molecular Microbiology |date=2007 |volume=66 |issue=4 |pages=872–889 |doi=10.1111/j.1365-2958.2007.05957.x}}</ref>

Braun conducted a genetic analysis of the ''fec'' region, which encodes a ferric dicitrate transport system of ''E. coli''. From this work, he described surface signaling, a form of transcriptional regulation that begins at the cell surface. It involves the transfer of a signal across the outer membrane, the periplasm and the cytoplasmic membrane into the cytoplasm without the ferric dicitrate itself getting inside the cell. His laboratory found that cells expressing truncated FecR derivatives no longer responded to ferric dicitrate and expressed the ''fec'' transport genes constitutively.<ref name="Crosa1997">{{cite journal |last1=Crosa |first1=JH |title=Signal transduction and transcriptional and posttranscriptional control of iron-regulated genes in bacteria |journal=Microbiology and Molecular Biology Reviews |date=1997 |volume=61 |issue=3 |pages=319–336 |doi=10.1128/mmbr.61.3.319-336.1997|quote=Cells expressing truncated...genes constitutively|pmc=232614 }}</ref> In the model developed on the basis of this study, ferric citrate binds the outer membrane receptor FecA, whose periplasmic N-terminal portion interacts with FecR at the cytoplasmic membrane, and FecR in turn activates the cytoplasmic sigma factor FecI by increasing its affinity for RNA polymerase.<ref name="Visca2002">{{cite journal |last1=Visca |first1=P |last2=Leoni |first2=L |last3=Wilson |first3=MJ |last4=Lamont |first4=IL |title=Iron transport and regulation, cell signalling and genomics: lessons from Escherichia coli and Pseudomonas |journal=Molecular Microbiology |date=2002 |volume=45 |issue=5 |pages=1177–1190 |doi=10.1046/j.1365-2958.2002.03088.x|quote=A wealth of evidence...cytoplasmic sigma factor FecI.}}</ref><ref name="Llamas2014" /> In later work, Braun proposed that the signal crosses the inner membrane through proteolysis of FecR by RseP, which is an enzyme of the sigma E activation pathway.<ref name="Brooks2008">{{cite journal |last1=Brooks |first1=BE |last2=Buchanan |first2=SK |title=Signaling mechanisms for activation of extracytoplasmic function (ECF) sigma factors |journal=Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - Biomembranes |date=2008 |volume=1778 |issue=9 |pages=1930–1945 |doi=10.1016/j.bbamem.2007.06.005|quote=Suggest that the signal...the σE activation pathway.|pmc=2562455 }}</ref>

Braun and colleagues described colicin M, a 28 kDa TonB-dependent colicin, in the 1970s, and used competition experiments with FhuA-dependent phages to show that it requires energy to cross the outer membrane, as do colicins B and Ib, while the Tol-dependent colicin E1 does not.<ref name="Cascales2007">{{cite journal |last1=Cascales |first1=E |last2=Buchanan |first2=SK |last3=Duché |first3=D |last4=Kleanthous |first4=C |last5=Lloubès |first5=R |last6=Postle |first6=K |last7=Riley |first7=M |last8=Slatin |first8=S |last9=Cavard |first9=D |title=Colicin biology |journal=Microbiology and Molecular Biology Reviews |date=2007 |volume=71 |issue=1 |pages=158–229 |doi=10.1128/MMBR.00036-06|quote=The group of Volkmar Braun...to cross the OM|pmc=1847374 }}</ref> With Holger Pilsl he compared the closely related colicins E1 and 10 to establish where the specificity for Tol-dependent or TonB-dependent uptake resides, and concluded that the TolC binding region must lie downstream of the TolA binding sequences.<ref name="Jakes2016">{{cite journal |last1=Jakes |first1=KS |title=The colicin E1 TolC box: identification of a domain required for colicin E1 cytotoxicity and TolC binding |journal=Journal of Bacteriology |date=2017 |volume=199 |issue=1 |page=e00412-16 |doi=10.1128/JB.00412-16|quote=Pilsl and Braun had...TolC for uptake|pmc=5165097 }}</ref> His laboratory also showed that the hemolysin ShlA of ''[[Serratia marcescens]]'' is modified as it is secreted through the outer membrane protein ShlB, which activates it through a conformational change,<ref name="Huber2022">{{cite journal |last1=Huber |first1=Philippe |title=ExlA: a new contributor to Pseudomonas aeruginosa virulence |journal=Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology |date=2022 |volume=12 |page=929150 |doi=10.3389/fcimb.2022.929150 |doi-access=free|quote=Braun's lab showed...through ShlB.|pmc=9260685 }}</ref> and that cells grown at 37 °C lysed erythrocytes approximately ten times less than cells grown at 30 °C, the result of which can be attributed to lipopolysaccharide structure and decreased levels of ShlB.<ref name="Abdulwahhab2022">{{cite journal |last1=Abdulwahhab |first1=AM |last2=Khalaf |first2=KJ |title=Effect of cultivation conditions on hemolysin production from clinical isolates of Serratia marcescens |journal=Al-Mustansiriyah Journal of Science |date=2022 |volume=33 |issue=1 |pages=6–14 |doi=10.23851/mjs.v33i1.1080|quote=Bacterial cells cultured...membrane protein ShlB at 37°C|doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Awards and honours ==
* 1982 – Main Prize (Hauptpreis), German Society for Hygiene and Microbiology<ref name="DGHM">{{cite book |title=1906–2006: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Hygiene und Mikrobiologie |date=2006 |publisher=Deutsche Gesellschaft für Hygiene und Mikrobiologie |language=de |url=https://www.dghm.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/festschrift-100-jahre-dghm.pdf}}</ref>
* 1994 – [[Robert Koch Prize]], Robert Koch Foundation<ref name="RKS">{{cite web |title=Preisträger:innen A - Z |url=https://www.robert-koch-stiftung.de/preise/preistraeger-a-z |publisher=Robert-Koch-Stiftung |language=de |access-date=11 September 2026}}</ref>
* 1998 – Ordinary member, [[Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities]]<ref name="HAdW" />
* 2005 – Honorary doctorate (Dr. med. honoris causa), Faculty of Medicine, [[University of Würzburg]]<ref name="HAdW" /><ref name="Wuerzburg">{{cite web |title=Prizes and honours |url=https://www.med.uni-wuerzburg.de/en/faculty/prizes-and-honours/ |publisher=Faculty of Medicine, University of Würzburg |access-date=11 September 2026}}</ref>
* 2008 – Member, [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]]<ref name="Leo2008" />
